objective: Add an immutable, evidence-bearing domain contract that separates survey-native object identifiers from astrophysical source identities and records explicit association states. No cross-match algorithm, automatic merge, persistence layer, or inference behavior is introduced.
previous_knowledge_consumed: Issue #249 and Issue #253 source identity and DR24 application boundaries
Existing domain Observation, CatalogMatch, CatalogContext and DiscoveryCandidate contracts.

baseline.description: Additive domain contract only. No existing observation, model, feature, taxonomy, benchmark, data or inference behavior changes.

expected_improvement: Make survey object and astrophysical source identity distinct in typed domain records.
Preserve survey, release, OID, band, field and rcid without rewriting native identifiers.
Represent confirmed, ambiguous, unmatched, rejected and deferred associations explicitly.
Require evidence and policy versions for confirmed associations.
Distinguish raw match scores from calibrated probabilities.
Prevent final unmatched, ambiguous, rejected or confirmed decisions from being recorded without evidence; allow DEFERRED_REVIEW to represent work not yet adjudicated.

correctness.before: The domain layer had normalized Observation contracts and catalog context records, but no dedicated source identity/association lifecycle types.
correctness.after: New frozen dataclasses define survey object, catalog entry, astrophysical source reference, association evidence and source association decision states.

reproducibility.reason: No matching algorithm, source registry persistence or external data execution is included.

scientific_validity.reason: The contracts do not establish physical identity. No adjudicated matching sample or independent cross-match evaluation is run.

measurement.trade_off: The first implementation intentionally stops at immutable records and validation. It does not calculate matches, merge OIDs, assign physical identity, or feed grouped observations to the model.

evidence: Added src/ztf_classifier/domain/source_identity.py with enum and frozen dataclass contracts.
Exported the new types from ztf_classifier.domain.

Added tests/test_source_identity_contracts.py covering native OID preservation, band-specific OID separation, catalog release scoping, provenance, association-state invariants and calibrated-score semantics.
No runtime call sites were changed.

Added 20 focused unit tests covering source-native OID preservation, distinct band-specific OIDs, catalog release scoping, source provenance, supersession lineage, score/probability semantics, confirmed/ambiguous/unmatched/rejected states, competing candidates, duplicate refs and self-supersession.

First CI run on the initial source identity head exposed one Ruff SIM102 lint finding; it was fixed in commit 6e33ba811ac49dea6b328b9e5eb8fb80077828b3. The corrected head requires a fresh full CI run.
Extended the contract to require evidence for all final association outcomes except DEFERRED_REVIEW, and to reject self-supersession of a source record.
Added three more tests: final association decisions require evidence; deferred review may wait for evidence; source records cannot supersede themselves.

CI run 43181774988 reached the cumulative lifecycle validator and failed before test execution. Exact validator output: unsupported metric name 'regression'; regression.status must be PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED or NOT_VERIFIED; decision must be ACCEPT, REVISE or BLOCKED.

Root cause was the lifecycle record schema, not a reported unit-test failure: regression was incorrectly duplicated under measurement.metrics, and PENDING_CI/PENDING_REVIEW are not accepted lifecycle values. The record is corrected by removing the unsupported metric entry and recording an honest BLOCKED state pending a fresh run.
validation.blocker: Fresh current-head CI is required after this lifecycle schema correction. The initial validator failure is retained and is not reported as a pass.

root_causes: Existing Observation.oid and CatalogMatch records do not represent a complete canonical identity lifecycle.
Without explicit association status, downstream code could treat source-native survey IDs as physical-source IDs.

First CI Lint run failed on Ruff SIM102 in the nested separation_arcsec validation condition. The condition was combined into one boolean expression in commit 6e33ba811ac49dea6b328b9e5eb8fb80077828b3.

Current lifecycle validation failed because the cycle JSON used unsupported metric name 'regression', regression.status='PENDING_CI', and decision='PENDING_REVIEW'. The repository validator accepts regression statuses PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT_VERIFIED and decisions ACCEPT/REVISE/BLOCKED.
unresolved: No source matching algorithm is implemented.
No append-only identity decision ledger or persistence store is implemented.
No adjudicated astrometric cross-match dataset or calibration study exists.
No DR24 application source selection or multi-OID grouping behavior is changed.

findings: A survey object OID is a source-native catalog identifier, not proof of physical source identity.
A confirmed association requires explicit source ID, supporting evidence and policy version.
Ambiguous, unmatched, rejected and deferred associations must remain explicit.
A raw matching score is not a probability. Calibrated probability requires a calibration version and bounded value.
This contract is additive and must not change the frozen v0.2.0 baseline or historical identifiers.

open_blockers: Corrected lifecycle record must pass cumulative validation on a fresh current-head CI run.
The 20 focused source-identity contract tests and full CI suite must pass on the corrected head.
Public API naming and compatibility require review before integration into ObservationService or DR24 application requests.

knowledge_carried_forward: Issue #249 remains the canonical source identity/AOIC tracker.
The new contracts do not implement or claim source matching.
No OID may be merged solely by angular proximity.
DR24 raw acquisition remains separate from model-ready normalized observations.
Initial CI run 43181774988 failed only at lifecycle-record validation before the test suite; exact cause and correction are recorded above. A fresh current-head CI run is required.
